A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpikeFET work, and their text, equations, figures and tables are readable. v1 ends after the references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 supplies Appendices A-I. The supplied documents support comparison of the retained content and newly documented material.

before.justification: Tables 1-4 report original SpikeFET and SpikeET tracking results and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original tracking results and reports additional input-count and loss-weight ablations, GPU runtimes, qualitative examples and layer firing rates.

M1.justification: The dual-single-dual architecture, RPM, STR, response loss and inference fusion remain unchanged. The appendix explains previously referenced SFA and CSWin-SSA components, while Section 3.4 clarifies first-frame template duplication; these disclosures do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 newly reports ImageNet-1K pretraining for SpikeFET-Tiny and SpikeET, whereas v1 describes pretraining through frame-tracking datasets. FE108, VisEvent and COESOT remain the evaluation datasets, and the previously named tracking-pretraining datasets remain represented for Base. No new tracking task or evaluation domain is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes DiMP50 from the reported event-only FE108 comparison: its 57.1 AUC and 85.1 PR entries become dashes, although it remains a VisEvent comparator. Other comparator memberships are retained. Table 1's new early-fusion and pretraining markers disclose comparator settings rather than introduce new methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds four-input controls alongside six-input configurations, alpha/beta sweeps, and an RTX 4090 FPS/MAC/AC evaluation. Section 4.1 also narrows the previously general tracking-dataset pretraining description to Base. Most newly stated splits, optimization settings and budgets document existing experiments; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds controls testing whether RPM's benefits persist with one template per modality. Appendix F adds sensitivity analyses for response-loss and STR weights, Appendix A adds COESOT tracking examples, and Table 11 supplies layer firing profiles relevant to efficiency. Together these substantially extend the original component and fusion ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests for the experimental results. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Headline SpikeFET/SpikeET tracking scores are retained, but v2 adds input-count and loss-weight results, baseline energy entries, runtime/operation counts and firing-rate measurements. Tables 9-10 report 106, 49.26 and 185.87 FPS for Tiny, Base and SpikeET respectively. DiMP50's event-only FE108 scores are removed. Table 10 also reports SDTrack FE108 AUC as 66.56, contradicting 59.9 in both versions' Table 2; this is an unresolved reporting discrepancy, not a verified performance or ranking change.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds an explicit firing-rate assumption and an integer-activation-to-spike-sequence derivation, while Appendix E supplies stripe/head definitions and a no-directional-bias assumption. These are limited formal additions for existing components. The original method equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: a first fully spiking unified frame-event tracker, RPM for padding-induced positional bias, STR for feature consistency, and favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs. Additional documentation and experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 expands the interpretation of VisEvent underperformance around scenario difficulty and dataset size, attributes gains primarily to RPM using the new input-count controls, and explains failure regimes for excessive or insufficient loss weights. Appendix I retains the pretraining limitation already discussed in v1 and identifies neuromorphic deployment as future work. The new 17.4-point VisEvent comparison uses different test subsets, limiting that interpretation.

D1.justification: v1 directs readers to an absent appendix for important details. v2 supplies SFA, event representation, response-loss and attention specifications; architecture and training hyperparameters in Tables 5-6; energy-estimation formulas and assumptions; and explicit VisEvent preprocessing and 320-versus-172 test-set distinctions. It also clarifies inference templates and provides a code/model repository link in place of a future-release promise. These substantially improve documented reproducibility without establishing corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: All 55 original references are retained, and nine works are added, including ImageNet and sources supporting spiking activations, event representations and energy estimation. The appendix adds some positioning against alternative representations, but Section 2 and the central novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on implementation and results explanations, a new Datasets subsection, explicit appendix cross-references, and author/publication information. The abstract's scientific content, introduction, related work, core method narrative and conclusion are largely retained. The supplement organizes substantial additional content without a wholesale rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds qualitative Figures 7-8 and Tables 5-11, including a multi-page firing-rate table. Table 3 gains an Inputs column and two configurations, Table 2 is enlarged, Table 1 gains explanatory markers, and Figure 1 labels its horizontal axis as theoretical power. Existing method figures are retained, with some relocated through the revised layout.

improvement.justification: v1 relies on an absent appendix for essential implementation and energy-estimation details. v2 supplies these, documents model-specific pretraining and evaluation subsets, and adds controls and runtime evidence, substantially improving reproducibility and scrutiny of the efficiency claims. The contradictory SDTrack AUC values in Tables 2 and 10 and the new comparison across different VisEvent subsets weaken parts of the reporting. These require correction, but the substantial gains in accessible methods and supporting evidence establish a net overall improvement.
